observations: Photo 0 shows a black DSLR with 'Nikon' on the prism and 'D3400' on the top right, with an AF-P lens mounted, resting on a 'McSteve Gadget Store' box.
Photo 1 shows the lens marked 'Nikon AF-P DX NIKKOR 70-300mm' and the camera body marked 'D3400', with the mode dial visible.
Photo 2 shows the same Nikon D3400 body with visible scuffing and wear on the left grip area, and the same 70-300mm lens.

claims.claim: Used Nikon D3400 DSLR Camera With 70-300mm Lens
claims.evidence: Nikon D3400 branding and 70-300mm lens markings are visible in photos 0, 1, and 2.

claims.claim: working perfectly ok with no fault
claims.evidence: Photos cannot show camera or lens function.
Photos 0, 1, and 2 all show Nikon branding, not Canon.

risks.risk: Camera body does not function (shutter, sensor, electronics, controls)
risks.proof: Video of the camera powering on, navigating menus, taking a photo, and reviewing the image.

risks.risk: Lens does not function (zoom, focus, aperture, image quality)
risks.proof: Video of the lens zooming through 70-300mm and focusing, plus sample photos taken through it.

risks.risk: High shutter count or hidden internal wear
risks.proof: Photo of the camera info screen showing shutter count.

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, navigating menus, and taking a photo
Video of the lens zooming and focusing
Photo of the camera info screen showing shutter count
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Nikon D3400 with a 70-300mm lens from the photos; the seller's claim that the brand is Canon is contradicted by visible Nikon branding, and functionality cannot be verified remotely so it is priced at its worst case as not working.
